summary: This bill amends the tax code so that people paying a fixed periodic fee for direct primary or specialty care from a doctor or nurse practitioner can still qualify for and use health savings accounts, by excluding those arrangements from counting as other health coverage and allowing the fees as HSA expenses.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to government spending, appropriations, or outlays. It solely amends the Internal Revenue Code regarding HSA eligibility and reporting.

The bill amends IRC sections 223 and 6051 to expand HSA eligibility for direct primary care arrangements and treat related fees as qualified medical expenses. This expands access to tax-advantaged accounts without raising taxes, producing a modest pro-tax-benefit effect.

The core purpose is to remove regulatory barriers so that direct medical care service arrangements (a market-based, subscription-style model) remain compatible with HSAs. This directly advances private, consumer-driven healthcare options over traditional insurance mandates.
